### ⭐ North Star gate — clause 3, re-taken for THIS claim

Reading taken at **2026-09-19T01:21Z**, by open-issue enumeration per repo (pull requests excluded), against `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` on `objectstack-ai/objectstack` `origin/main` `5eebc9edced6d74fe6c76c76bab7c8483bdcfbbb`:

| product repo (reading taken 2026-09-19T01:21Z) | open P0 | open P1 |
|---|---|---|
| objectstack-ai/objectstack | 4 | 47 |
| objectstack-ai/objectui | 0 | 8 |

⇒ the gate is **CLOSED**. Clause 3 reads: 「产品仓还有开放的 P0/P1 时,任何车道不派 p2/p3 的工具卡、契约卫生卡;解锁产品 P0/P1 的仪器卡沿链继承其优先级」.

⭐ This card passes the gate because it is **neither**. It is a `priority:p2` **product** card: an author writes a `sort`, the grid renders unordered, and the console says nothing. Clause 2 grades that exactly — 「能跑但出错 ⇒ P2」— and clause 4 is the one it violates by name: 「错的必须被响亮拒绝并给处方,永不静默落库」. ⛔ It is not a tool card (it changes no gate, script or ratchet) and ⛔ not contract hygiene (it changes no declared shape — see the fence in §3, which is the whole point).

### 1. The defect, re-measured at source by this seat

Read on objectui `origin/main` **`8a7e09fa158a01889607b46c855879e99fc29415`** (freshly fetched at claim time), `packages/core/src/utils/sort-query.ts`. The filing seat used `272a53066` / `d6a84446f`; triage used `05a49f2eed`; this is a fourth, later ref and the finding still stands.

`normalizeSortEntries` has exactly two arms after the `!sort` guard:

```ts
if (typeof (sort as unknown) === 'string') {          // scalar retired spelling
  reportRetiredSortSpelling(sort as unknown as string);   // ← LOUD
  return undefined;
}

if (Array.isArray(sort)) {
  const out: NormalizedSortEntry[] = [];
  for (const entry of sort) {
    if (!entry || typeof entry.field !== 'string' || entry.field === '') continue;   // ← SILENT
    out.push({ field: entry.field, order: entry.order === 'desc' ? 'desc' : 'asc' });
  }
  return out.length > 0 ? out : undefined;
}
```

A string entry such as `'name asc'` has no `field` property, so `typeof entry.field !== 'string'` is true and the entry falls through `continue`. Every entry of an all-strings array does the same, `out.length` is 0, the function returns `undefined`, the query carries no `$orderby` — and **nothing is printed**. The scalar spelling of the same intent, one arm above, prints a full prescription. That is the card's middle row, re-derived from the source rather than re-run as a probe.

Control from the same read, so the silence is not a reading artefact: `reportRetiredSortSpelling` exists and is reached — it is called on line 1 of the first arm — and `retired` occurs on **7** lines of this file. The instrument (a diagnostic sink in this module) is lit; it simply is not wired to this arm.

### 2. ⛔ The card's one open question is already answered — by a ruling, not by a judgement call

The filing seat wrote: ⚠️ NOT MEASURED — 「the fix's shape (emit the existing retired-spelling diagnostic for this arm, **or accept and normalise the spelling**) is the claiming seat's measurement」.

This seat measured it, in this act, from the file's own docblock (`sort-query.ts`, the module header):

> The legacy OData-ish string clause (`"name desc"`) that this function also honoured until objectui#8221 is RETIRED — **director ruling, decision batch #77, 2026-09-07 (objectui#8221, maintainer approved), option B: "The platform has one `sort` spelling, the array, everywhere."**

⇒ the second branch — accept and normalise `['name asc']` — is **barred**. It would re-admit the retired spelling one container deeper, and the ruling that retired it is maintainer-approved and names option A (per-block string arms) as rejected by name. ⛔ Do not take it. The fix shape is therefore settled before dispatch: **emit a diagnostic, change no accepted input**.

### 3. ⭐ The fence, stated now so the fix is not mis-sized

The same docblock also says, four paragraphs above the loud-refusal paragraph:

> Not a lenient alias: an unusable input (a number, an object, **an array of strings**) yields `undefined` rather than a guess.

⚠️ These two sentences are **not** in conflict and a dev must not "resolve" them. The first governs the RETURN VALUE (`undefined`, no guess) and stays true. The second governs the DIAGNOSTIC (「REFUSED OUT LOUD, not dropped in silence」) and is the one being violated. Being loud is not the same as accepting. The correct end state is: array-of-strings still yields `undefined`, and now also says why.

⛔ Equally out of scope: the `entry.field` skip itself. The docblock declares it deliberately — 「an entry with no usable `field` is SKIPPED (it names nothing to order by)」 — so an entry-shaped object missing `field` keeps today's silence. The seam is `typeof entry === 'string'`, and only that.

⛔ And the empty-array case is a different card, already closed: objectui#9607, closed by this seat as a measured no-op. ⛔ Do not fold it in.

### 4. Staleness — three faces, all read in this act

- **动作面** — `git log --oneline -20 origin/main -- packages/core/src/utils/sort-query.ts` returns exactly one commit, `f73521f93` (a `tsconfig.test.json` docblock dating, objectui#9750). ⇒ nobody has touched the arm since the card was filed; the defect is live on today's tip.
- **卡引用面** — objectui#9607 read on GitHub in this act: `closed`. objectui#8221's ruling is quoted above from the file, not from memory.
- **工作项面** — 14 open PRs in this repo enumerated at claim time; none names `sort-query.ts` or `packages/core/src/utils/**`. No in-flight writer on this file.

### 5. In-flight file-face intersection — declared

This seat's other two in-flight cards and their faces: **#9978** → `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/normalize-list-view.pageResidual-8429.test.ts`; **#9979** → `packages/core/src/validation/__tests__/object-validation-engine.test.ts`. Both PRs (objectui#9982, objectui#9981) are in the merge queue at claim time.

⇒ #9978 shares the **directory** `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/` with this card's likely test site but ⛔ not a file. No intersection, no serialization owed. This card's declared face:

```
packages/core/src/utils/sort-query.ts
packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/sort-query.test.ts
.changeset/*
```

### 6. Prior rulings

`Prior rulings read: sort,orderby,retired spelling,sort-query → 2 hits; ADR-0029 D9.3, ADR-0061 D4`

Both read: ADR-0029 D9.3 is kernel-object selection by KIND, ADR-0061 D4 is server-side label↔value ranking for record search. ⛔ Neither answers this card's question. The governing ruling is objectui#8221, quoted in §2.

## Dispatch — one `os-dev`, one worktree

Issued at 2026-09-19T01:26Z by `domain:ui#2` (`session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`). Base: objectui `origin/main` `8a7e09fa158a01889607b46c855879e99fc29415` at issue time — ⛔ re-fetch and branch from whatever `origin/main` is when you start, and re-take every reading below against YOUR base.

### ⭐ Provenance of every assertion in this order

Two kinds only, and they are labelled inline:
- **[SEAT-MEASURED]** — this seat read it at source in the claim act, on `origin/main` `8a7e09fa1`. Re-take it on your base; if it differs, that difference is the report, not a nuisance.
- **[CARD-CLAIM]** — the filing seat's or triage's reading, relayed. ⛔ Do not build on it until you have re-measured it yourself.

### 1. What is wrong

**[SEAT-MEASURED]** In `packages/core/src/utils/sort-query.ts`, `normalizeSortEntries` has two arms after the `!sort` guard. The scalar retired spelling is loud:

```ts
if (typeof (sort as unknown) === 'string') {
  reportRetiredSortSpelling(sort as unknown as string);
  return undefined;
}
```

The array arm is silent about the same mistake one container deeper:

```ts
for (const entry of sort) {
  if (!entry || typeof entry.field !== 'string' || entry.field === '') continue;
  out.push({ field: entry.field, order: entry.order === 'desc' ? 'desc' : 'asc' });
}
return out.length > 0 ? out : undefined;
```

A string entry (`'name asc'`) has no `field`, so it hits `continue`. An all-strings array leaves `out` empty, returns `undefined`, and the query carries no `$orderby` — with zero diagnostics.

**[CARD-CLAIM]** The three-leg runtime probe in the issue body (`retired-diagnostics` 1 / 0 / 0 across scalar-string, array-of-strings, declared-array) was run by the objectui#9607 dev, ⛔ not by this seat. ⛔ Do not quote its numbers as yours. If you want a runtime reading, run your own and say so.

### 2. What the fix is — and the one thing it must NOT be

**[SEAT-MEASURED]** The module docblock quotes the governing ruling verbatim:

> The legacy OData-ish string clause (`"name desc"`) that this function also honoured until objectui#8221 is RETIRED — director ruling, decision batch #77, 2026-09-07 (objectui#8221, maintainer approved), option B: "The platform has one `sort` spelling, the array, everywhere."

⇒ **⛔ Do not accept or normalise `['name asc']`.** Making it work would re-admit the retired spelling one level down and reverse a maintainer-approved ruling. The accepted input set does ⛔ not change, by one key or one shape.

**The fix is the diagnostic and nothing else.** End state: an array entry that is a `string` still yields no `$orderby`, and now prints a prescription naming the array form — the same class of message `reportRetiredSortSpelling` already prints for the scalar.

**[SEAT-MEASURED]** The two docblock sentences that look contradictory are not, and ⛔ neither may be edited away:
- 「Not a lenient alias: an unusable input (a number, an object, **an array of strings**) yields `undefined` rather than a guess.」 — governs the RETURN VALUE. Stays true after your change.
- 「A retired string is REFUSED OUT LOUD, not dropped in silence … Returning `undefined` and saying nothing would turn every one of those into a row order that quietly stopped applying」 — governs the DIAGNOSTIC. This is the one being violated.

Loud ≠ accepted. If your diff makes the first sentence false, you built the wrong thing.

### 3. Scope fence — three things that are ⛔ NOT this card

1. **The `field`-less object entry.** **[SEAT-MEASURED]** `normalizeSortEntries`' own docblock declares it: 「an entry with no usable `field` is SKIPPED (it names nothing to order by)」. That silence is designed. ⛔ Leave it. The seam you are adding is `typeof entry === 'string'`, and only that.
2. **The empty array.** **[SEAT-MEASURED]** objectui#9607, read on GitHub in the claim act: `closed`, by this seat, as a measured no-op. ⛔ Do not fold it in.
3. **The wire shape.** **[SEAT-MEASURED]** The docblock records that swapping `object-grid`'s `"field order"` join string for this module's map is route B on objectui#8767, **declined by the maintainer by name (2026-09-10)**. ⛔ Nowhere near this card.

### 4. Points you decide, with the reading that has to back each

- **Where the message is emitted.** `reportRetiredSortSpelling(sort: string)` takes the whole value and dedupes on it through the module-level `reportedRetiredSpellings` set. A per-entry string needs either that function reused with the entry as its key, or a sibling. ⛔ Whichever you pick, say in the PR what the dedupe key becomes and why a page with N blocks inheriting one bad view still prints a bounded number of lines — the existing dedupe exists for exactly that reason and its docblock says so.
- **Mixed arrays.** `[{field:'a',order:'asc'}, 'b desc']` must still order by `a`. Assert it.
- **The message text.** **[SEAT-MEASURED]** The existing scalar message is a worked example, not a complaint: it names `ARRAY_FORM_EXAMPLE = "[{ field: 'name', order: 'desc' }]"`, states that `order` is REQUIRED at publish, and states that a missing `order` is a runtime tolerance and ⛔ not permission to omit it. objectui#9031 is the card that put both halves there. ⛔ Do not write a message that prescribes metadata a publish refuses, and ⛔ do not drop the tolerance sentence — its docblock says both halves are load-bearing and both must survive any rewording.
- **`console.error`, not `warn`, and not dev-gated.** **[SEAT-MEASURED]** The existing sink's docblock argues that choice explicitly against two named siblings (`reportRetiredFieldType` unconditional, `warnOnUnknownActionKeys` dev-only). Match it, or argue in the PR why this arm is a different severity class.

### 5. Tests

**[SEAT-MEASURED]** `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/sort-query.test.ts` exists on the base. Extend it; ⛔ do not start a parallel file.

`resetRetiredSortSpellingReports()` is exported precisely so a second assertion does not observe the dedupe's silence and pass for the wrong reason — its docblock says so. Use it between cases.

⭐ Every new assertion needs a **lit control in the same test body**, or it is not a reading:
- subject: an all-strings `sort` ⇒ returns `undefined` **and** the sink fired once;
- control A (must stay loud): the scalar `'name asc'` ⇒ the existing diagnostic, unchanged;
- control B (must stay silent AND work): `[{field:'name',order:'desc'}]` ⇒ a map, no diagnostic;
- control C (must stay silent — the designed skip): `[{order:'asc'}]` ⇒ `undefined`, **no** diagnostic. ⭐ This is the one that proves you cut the seam at `typeof entry === 'string'` and not at "entry has no field".
- mixed: `[{field:'a',order:'asc'}, 'b desc']` ⇒ orders by `a`, and the sink fired for `'b desc'`.

### 6. Declared file face

```
packages/core/src/utils/sort-query.ts
packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/sort-query.test.ts
.changeset/*
```

⛔ Anything outside this face is a stop-and-report, not a rider. **[SEAT-MEASURED]** 14 open PRs enumerated at claim time; none touches `packages/core/src/utils/**`, so you have the file to yourself — but re-check at branch time.

### 7. Stop conditions — a stop with evidence is a good outcome, ⛔ not a failure

- The array arm already prints something on your base ⇒ stop, report what and since when.
- The only way you can see to make it loud also changes what input is accepted ⇒ stop and report. §2 is a ruling, not a preference.
- Your reading of the two docblock sentences contradicts §2 ⇒ stop and report, with the lines.

### 8. Deliverable

Branch, code, tests, changeset, push, **draft** PR with `Fixes #9955`. ⛔ Do not flip it out of draft, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ do not merge — landing is this seat's act after review. Report back as structured JSON.

In the PR body: the before/after of the three-arm behaviour with the controls above, the dedupe-key decision from §4, and an explicit line stating that the accepted input set is unchanged.
